## Learning Objectives {.objectives}

-   Assess your project's lottery factor and identify single points of failure.
-   Write a one-page advance directive for your project.
-   Begin a succession plan for your own role.

## The Lottery Factor

-   How many people have to be unavailable in order for the project to halt?
-   Most research projects have a lottery factor of one for most functions.
-   Most leads do not find out until the person leaves.

## Preparing for Transitions

-   Preparing for a transition means making project health independent of individuals.
    -   Grant cycles give succession planning a natural calendar.
-   Minimum version for an ongoing project has three parts:
    -   A shared credentials document.
    -   A release checklist.
    -   An advance directive.

## If It Happens

-   Don't announce shutdown immediately.
-   Instead, announce that you are stopping work and invite people you know to take over.
    -   Only people you know because of the risk of supply chain attacks.
-   If no one is willing to take over, try to give users 2-6 months.
-   Broadcast on all available channels.
-   Tell people why, and what will happen to the project's assets.
